lawyer:
JK Paul with Banamali Nandi, Advocates—For the Petitioner. 
Abdul Mannan Khan with Abdul Wahab, Advocates—For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Narayan Dash ------ Petitioner.
Vs.
Md Mostofa and ors ------ Opposite Parties.
full_judgment:
Opposite Party No. 1 was called upon to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 5-9-2005 and 8-9-2005 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Second Court, Noakhali in Title Appeal No. 147 of 2003 reversing the judgment and decree dated 31-5-2003 and 7-6-2003 respectively passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Begumganj, Noakhali in Title Suit No. 156 of 2002 should not be set aside. 

 6. In consideration of the evidence trial Court dismissed the suit. Plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No. 147 of 2003 in the Court of the learned District Judge, Noakhali against the said judgment and decree. The learned Additional District Judge, Second Court, Noakhali heard and allowed the appeal on contest decreeing the suit setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court. Hence this Rule. 

 7. Trial Court dismissed the suit on the finding that the plaintiff remained absent from 1-5-1997 and he failed to explain his conduct and did not join the school despite issuance of 3rd show cause notice by the Managing Committee of the school thus removed him from service on 14-6-1997 and thereafter, appointed the defendant No. 1 as Headmaster of the school. Trial Court further found that the plaintiff could not prove by any documentary evidence that he was granted leave for 2 years from 1-5-1997 to 30-4-1999, his application for leave and leave granting order not examined by any other witness in support of his case. Trial Court also found that the plaintiff failed to prove that the defendant No. 1 was appointed as Headmaster of the school illegally, without requisite qualification and experience. Appellate Court below, in decreeing the suit reversing and setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court, found that DW 1 himself admitted in his cross examination that the School Committee in its meeting dated 20-4-1997 granted extraordinary leave for 2 years to the plaintiff from 1-5-1997 to 30-4-1999 under Article 21 of the Non-Government Secondary School Teachers (Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education Dhaka) Terms and Conditions of Service Regulation 1979 as amended up to 1999, hereinafter referred to as said resolution and neither any copy of show cause notice was issued to the plaintiff nor any evidence to that effect have been produced in the case. Appellate Court below also found that the resolution dated 14-6-1997 does not show that the plaintiff was given an opportunity of self-defense and that the order of removal of the plaintiff is against the principle of natural justice. Trial Court relied on the decision in the case of Rafiqul Alam vs Secretary, Ministry of Works, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and others reported in 49 DLR 456. 

 8. Mr JK Paul, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that the trial Court rightly dismissed the suit but the appellate Court below erred in law in decreeing the suit setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court erroneously without taking into consideration that the plaintiff is in service as Headmaster of another school from 1-12-1998. Mr. Paul further submits that the plaintiff being in service as Headmaster of another school from 1-12-1998 the suit filed by him on 3-11-1999 is not maintainable and the trial Court rightly dismissed the suit and the appellate Court judgment and decree is liable to be set aside for non-consideration of the same by the appellate Court below in passing his impugned judgment and decree. He also submits the decision referred by the appellate Court below is not applicable in the facts of the instant case. Mr Paul referred the appointment letter of the plaintiff as Headmaster of another school and some other papers in same regard in support of his submission enclosed with the counter-affidavit marked Annexures X(1), X(2) and X(3) submitted against an application filed by plaintiff for vacating the order of stay passed by this court at the time of issuance of the Rule. 

 9. On the other hand, Mr Abdul Wahab, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No. 1, submits that the appellate Court below after proper discussion of the relevant evidence and upon consideration of the same decreed the suit setting aside the trial Court judgment and decree. Mr Wahab contends that the plaintiff was not given any opportunity in his self-defence by issuing show cause notice to him and defendant could not produce any evidence to that effect and upon consideration of the same the appellate Court below rightly decreed the suit in part finding that the impugned removal order is against the principle of natural justice. He also submits that the Annexures X(1), X(2) and X(3) being not evidence and beyond the pleading, the Rule cannot be made absolute on the basis of those Annexures. He argues that the defendant No. 1 having admitted in his cross-examination that the plaintiff was granted extra-ordinary leave and the defendant having failed to produce any evidence to show that the plaintiff was on unauthorized leave and that the School Committee's issuance of show cause notice to him, appellate Court below rightly decreed the suit, etc. 

 10. Perused the judgment and decree of the court below, counter affidavit, affidavit-in-reply to the same, etc. filed by the parties and heard the learned Advocates of both the sides. 

 14. Mr JK Paul, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, did not controvert the same at all. On the other hand, Mr Paul has referred some papers enclosed as Annexure-X(1), X(2) and X(3) with his counter-affidavit submitted by him in reply to an application filed by the defendant No. 1 for vacating the order of stay granted by the Court and submitted that the Rule may be made absolute on the basis of those papers which have not been considered by the appellate Court below. This submission of Mr Paul is ridiculous, The referred Exhibits X(1), X(2) X(3) are the same papers showing the appointment of the plaintiff in another school on 1-12-1998 as Headmaster to his application dated 15-11-1998, The papers are not at all evidence and cannot be used for making the Rule absolute setting aside the appellate Court judgment and decree. The plaintiff filed the suit on 3-11-1999 which has been contested by the defendant Nos. 1-12 but nowhere in their written statement there are any words referring Exhibits X(1), X(2) and X(3) nor the defendant produced those documents and led any evidence before any of the courts below. Trial Court dismissed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 31-5-2003 and the Appellate Court below decreed the suit by its judgment dated 5-9-2002 but instead of producing those papers before the court at any stage how the learned Advocate like JK Paul submits for making the Rule absolute at this stage on the basis of those papers is not understandable. Mr Paul having made no argument controverting the finding of the appellate Court below that the plaintiff have been punished unheard the removal order has offended the principle of natural justice. 

 15. The appellate Court below has rightly passed the impugned judgment and order decreeing the suit in part declaring the impugned removal order as illegal from the facts and evidence of the case. Appellate Court below having passed the judgment on proper discussion and due consideration of the evidence of the case I find no reason to disturb the same. I find no merit in the Rule which is liable to be discharged. 

 16. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. The judgment and decree of the appellate Court is hereby affirmed. The order of stay granted earlier by this court is hereby vacated.
